specFirst: Written per skills/agentsBestPractices.md §1. This file, spec.md and the per-step CHANGELOG.md are the design record. The decisions were closed with the product owner between 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-27 (recorded, section by section, in the control document on the author's machine — never cited by path here, per shared/localDocRefs.test.ts) and are restated in decisions[] below; when behaviour must change, change this file first, then the code.
description: Generates the molecule catalog an LLM consumer reads to choose components: l2/molecules/skill.ts (level 1, project) and, per group, index.defs.ts + index.html (level 2) — all 100% derivable, no LLM. E8 adds s3-indexts, which now has two modes: migrating a group's index.ts showcase page from its hand-authored scenario table to a thin call into a shared renderer (deterministic, no LLM — E8a, G3 groups), and creating an index.ts from scratch for a group that has none (E8b, G1 groups, the ONLY place this agent uses an LLM — one call per G1 group). Both modes plant the same s3-<group> step; which one runs is decided by whether the group's index.ts exists.
principles: THIS AGENT SPENDS NO LLM CALL EXCEPT s3's CREATION MODE (E8b), and even there it is exactly one call per G1 group, never a classifier deciding scope. Discovery, mention scoping (helpers/syEntry), and migration-vs-creation triggers (helpers/syMigrateIndexTs) are all deterministic. The root's own bootstrap step uses AgentIntentAddMessageAI.skipRootLLM — the same mechanism agentChangeFrontend already ships with — so the platform gets its step tree without a classifier deciding something that was never a classification. s3's migration mode (G3) also spends zero LLM calls; only creation mode (G1) does, and it is a single tool-call turn per group, the same shape as agentNewMolecule2's n7-index.

REUSE THE PLUMBING. Intents and l4 mechanics come from agentNewMolecule2/helpers (nmFs, nmSteps), the same way agentChooseMolecules reuses them. One new function was added to the shared nmFs.ts (nmGroupDefsFile) — a small, additive extension, not a fork.

THE TAG IS NEVER DERIVED FROM A FILENAME. It comes from the real `@customElement(...)` decorator of the molecule's own .ts (helpers/syExtract.syExtractTag) — the rule that got 45/45 tags right in the pilot.

SCENARIOS ARE THE ONE FIELD THAT IS NOT DERIVED. They are editorial. On a group's first sync they are harvested mechanically from its CURRENT index.ts (a data read, not composition — no LLM); on every later sync, whatever is already in the group's index.defs.ts is PRESERVED untouched. See decisions.scenarioHarvest.

GROUP -> PROJECT, NEVER IN PARALLEL. s2 (skill.ts) dependsOn every s1 (index.defs.ts) anchor of the run and reads their l4 artifacts, never level 2 source text directly. s3 (migration) dependsOn its OWN group's s1 anchor only — it needs index.defs.ts to exist before index.ts starts importing it, nothing from other groups.

HONESTY OVER SILENCE. A group with no skills/index.ts entry is IGNORED WITH A REASON, never dropped quietly (D4). The report always says the catalog is written but not published (D5, by impossibility — no publish API exists on this platform). Every matched group's index.ts status (migrated / needs creation / migration failed / already migrated) is reported by name — a run never reads as having silently skipped a page.

decisions.defaultLlmCost: Zero for every group, except a G1 group's index.ts creation (E8b): exactly one LLM tool-call turn per G1 group, spent by agentSyIndexTs itself in creation mode — no separate agent, no classifier. Measured: none of the pure helpers, agentSyGroup, agentSyProject or agentSyReport call an LLM, ever; agentSyIndexTs calls one only when its group has no index.ts at all (G1). Confirmed viable via a real precedent: mls-102020/l2/agentChangeFrontend/agentChangeFrontend.ts already ships AgentIntentAddMessageAI.skipRootLLM for exactly this purpose (the root bootstrap).
decisions.rootPlanting: Single phase, unlike agentChooseMolecules. That family needs two phases because the fan-out size (how many groups an LLM chose) is unknown until c1 answers. Here discovery is a stor scan the root itself can do synchronously in beforePromptImplicit, so every step (s1 x N, s3 x M, s2, s4) is planted in ONE batch, dependency edges included.
decisions.groupOrder: Alphabetical by folder — NOT skills/index.ts order. The first hypothesis (matched groups follow skills/index.ts's own order) fit 4 of the 6 seeded groups and was falsified by E5's regeneration: the seed's skill.ts lists 'groupViewTable' BEFORE 'groupEnterDate', the opposite of their skills/index.ts order. A second hypothesis (skills/index.ts order full stop) was also tried and also falsified. The seed's actual order looks like an artifact of the ad-hoc pilot seeding process, not a rule — alphabetical is simple, deterministic, and reproduces every OTHER structural property of the seed exactly.
decisions.purposeText: The FULL skills/index.ts `description`, untruncated, for both level 1 and level 2's 'Objetivo do grupo' line. The seed truncates it (drops a trailing 'Implementations include...' / 'Supports...' sentence in most groups, but keeps the WHOLE description for groupSelectOne, which has neither trigger phrase). Measured on 2026-08-25: skills/index.ts has been hand-edited since the pilot's 2026-08-21 seed, so no clean split-point formula reproduces all 6 groups from the CURRENT source text. Publishing the full description is simple, always in sync with the manually-maintained source of truth — a fragile truncation heuristic would be worse than a longer but always-accurate line.
decisions.scenarioHarvest: Not in the original E1-E7 helper list, but required by the ordering rule itself: s1 runs before s3, and s1 must write a complete index.defs.ts — including `scenarios` — even when s3 never runs. So the harvest lives in s1 (helpers/syExtract.syHarvestScenarios), reading the group's CURRENT index.ts. Table columns use free, abbreviated field names (`detailGrid`, `advanced`, plain `data` in groupViewTable; `mlDateIntervalDrag` keeping the 'ml' prefix in others) — matched to a molecule by TOKEN SET, not string similarity, in three tiers: (1) exact set match; (2) the unique SMALLEST superset (plain `data` is a subset of 5 `*-data-*` molecules; `ml-data-table` alone has no token beyond what the field named); (3) a unique squashed-substring match, for a compound word spelled as ONE word in the filename but split by camelCase in the field (`mindMap` vs `ml-view-hierarchy-mindmap`'s `mindmap`). A genuine tie at any tier is left unmatched, never guessed. E8 prep found and fixed two bugs in this matcher by sweeping all 30 real groups (D-E3, below) — 7 of 30 looked 'foreign' before the fixes, 1 after.
decisions.migrationIsAutomatic: SINCE E8, index.ts migration (G3) is NOT gated behind the mention's opt-in phrase anymore. E1-E7 treated all index.ts work as opt-in because it was assumed authorial and risky (up to 795 hand-written lines). E8's measurement (todo-implementar-E8-index-ts.md §1) showed migration is actually deterministic text surgery with a cheap, safe failure mode (the gate in helpers/syMigrateIndexTs.ts either applies cleanly or changes nothing) — so the asymmetric-cost argument for opt-in no longer applies to it, and it now runs automatically whenever a matched group has the G3 trigger. The opt-in phrase is still parsed and still recorded (SyRunInput.includeIndexTsRequested), because it still matters for a G1 group (creation, E8b, LLM) — not built, so a request for it gets an honest 'not built yet' from s4, never silence.
decisions.s3Migration_D-E1_sharedModuleLocation: D-E1 (closed with the product owner, 2026-08-25): the generic table-rendering code lives in mls-102020/l2/aura/molecules/shared/ (indexReferenceTable.ts + indexReferenceTableData.ts), imported FROM mls-102040's index.ts files — chosen over the alternative of putting it inside mls-102040 itself, or duplicating it per group. ⚠️ RISK NAMED AND ACCEPTED, NOT DISCOVERED AS SAFE: there is no existing precedent in this repo for mls-102040 source importing `/_102020_/` (only the reverse, and the unrelated `enhancement=` triple-slash metadata directive) — searched and confirmed absent. A scoped `tsc` compile of the migrated groupEnterDate/groupViewTable against the real shared module DID resolve cleanly (E8a acceptance, below), which is strong TYPE-LEVEL evidence, but the Studio's own runtime module/dependency resolution is a different system and was not exercised. If it does not resolve there, every migrated page's reference table breaks the same way, all at once, which is what makes it easy to notice and revert.
decisions.s3Migration_D-E2_color: D-E2 (closed): header color is derived from the molecule's ALPHABETICAL index in molecules[] (helpers/syLabels.syPaletteColor), not harvested from the pre-migration page's historical import-order pairing — a deliberate visual change, chosen over preserving the old color-per-tag mapping (which the product owner considered, but declined, given the coupled D-E2b below). Tailwind classes are a STATIC lookup table (shared/indexReferenceTableData.ts COLOR_CLASSES), never string-interpolated (`text-${color}-600`), because Tailwind's build scans literal source text for class names and a computed one is invisible to it.
decisions.s3Migration_D-E2b_columnOrder: Follow-up to D-E2, closed the same session: because color now comes from the alphabetical index, the COLUMN ORDER also became alphabetical (matching molecules[]) rather than staying in the page's historical order — otherwise colors would read as scattered instead of in a clean left-to-right sequence. This is why block ④ (the reference-table markup) could not stay literally untouched, which led directly to s3Migration_consolidation below.
decisions.s3Migration_consolidation: Once color+order already required editing the table's markup (D-E2b) and D-E1 already asked for a 'thin call site', the whole `renderReferenceTable()` method collapses to ~3 lines (`return renderCatalogReferenceTable(molecules, scenarios);`) instead of the ①②③-only surgery the todo originally scoped (leaving ④'s ~40-90 lines of markup in each group's own file). Confirmed explicitly with the product owner as a deliberate, bigger-than-originally-scoped simplification, not a unilateral expansion — the todo's own measurement (§1) that the markup is structurally IDENTICAL across groups is what makes unifying it lossless.
decisions.s3Migration_D-E3_foreignColumns: D-E3 (closed, WITH a real measurement, not an impression): swept all 30 real groups with an index.ts for scenario-table fields matching no LOCAL molecule (candidates for 'this recommends a molecule from another group'). Before fixing the two matcher bugs above: 7 of 30 groups, 19 columns. After: 1 of 30 (`groupEnterNumber`'s 'Range Slider' column, genuinely `ml-number-range-slider` from `groupEnterNumberInterval`). Decision: such a column never renders (the product owner's own constraint — 'nenhum index deve referenciar moléculas de outros grupos' — already rules out showing it), and a scenario row left with ZERO in-group recommendations after dropping it is OMITTED from the rendered table entirely (not shown as an all-empty row) — it stays in scenarios[] in the .defs.ts either way, so no data is lost, only a dead row is not drawn.
decisions.s3Migration_D-E4_title: D-E4 (closed): swept all 30 groups' `<h2>` reference-table title — 28 say 'Quick reference', 2 (`groupTriggerAction`, `groupViewTable`) say 'Referência rápida' (found during the sweep; the todo's own text only knew about groupViewTable). The shared module hardcodes 'Quick reference' for every group, normalizing both outliers. This is the one place the migration edits prose inside what used to be block ④ — accepted because it is a single, uniform, swept correction, not a per-group judgment call.
decisions.e8bCreation_targetChanged: todo-implementar-E8b-criar-index-ts.md §1 (closed with the product owner, 2026-08-27): creation is no longer '2 holes in mls-102040' (groupNavigateMain, groupEnterDateTime). Measured 2026-08-26: mls-102053 (a project that received molecules by COPY) has 7 of 7 groups as G1 — the copy brought the molecule files but not their showcase pages. Creation is now the normal case for any copied project, not an exception, and the root plants one s3 step per G1 group with no cap — same shape as G3/migration.
decisions.e8bCreation_sameStepTwoModes: s3-<group> stays ONE step/ONE agent (agentSyIndexTs) with two modes, decided by whether the group's index.ts exists when the step runs (nmFileExists) — not by a flag the root passes. Migration mode is unchanged: fully synchronous in beforePromptStep, no prompt_ready, ends in a completed result step (todo §0.4, 'não reabra o que já funciona'). Creation mode returns a prompt_ready intent instead and adds an afterPromptStep handler — a step with only beforePromptStep never reaches afterPromptStep on this platform (confirmed against every step-only agent in this family), so afterPromptStep is simply never invoked for a migration run. This avoids a parallel creation-only agent (which would fork the done-anchor/dependsOn wiring the root and s4 already have for s3) and avoids a mode flag that could desync from the actual file state.
decisions.e8bCreation_skillReuseNotFork: The system prompt reuses skills/indexGroupPage.ts VERBATIM (todo §2: 'Reuse a skill, não o agente') plus an appended '## OVERRIDE' section that supersedes only that skill's renderReferenceTable() instructions — never a forked copy of the skill with the table section hand-edited out. A forked copy is a second source of truth that silently drifts from the original the next time indexGroupPage.ts is edited for the two legacy agents (agentIndexGroupPage/agentUpdateIndexGroupPage) that still use it unmodified; an appended override does not.
decisions.e8bCreation_pageIsBornMigrated: todo §3, the sharpest failure mode named: the model must NOT hand-write rows/headers/<table> and have a later run 'fix' it. The OVERRIDE section in the prompt gives the exact 3-line renderReferenceTable() body and the two import lines verbatim (the same text syMigrateIndexTs.ts generates for E8a), and the gate (steps/s3-indexts/createGate.ts) fails the attempt — triggering the same retry loop as agentNewMolecule2's n7-index — if the body is not exactly that call, or if `<table`, `headers.map(`, or a `rows` array literal appear anywhere in the file. This is enforced structurally, not just requested in prose.
decisions.e8bCreation_scenariosAsData: todo §4 (correction of the same day — an earlier draft invented a false dilemma between 'derived' and 'authored' scenarios that does not exist): scenarios were ALWAYS authorial — skills/indexGroupPage.ts already told the model to hand-write the `rows`/`headers` arrays (line 106), and the pilot's seed HARVESTED that authored table, it never derived it. E8b keeps the model as the author; only the ADDRESS changes. The model returns `scenarios: Array<{ scenario, recommended }>` as a structured tool-call field (schemas/s3-indexts-create.schema.json) instead of Lit markup, `recommended` naming SHORT molecule names (matching the 'Available molecules' list the prompt already shows it, the same list it would have used to name componentA/componentB before). The step then converts short name -> full prefixed tag and writes it into the group's index.defs.ts scenarios[] — the model never touches that file directly.
decisions.e8bCreation_rewriteViaRendererNotTextEdi: todo §4 item 2: 'Reuse o renderizador do s1 (syRenderDefs) com os cenários novos, em vez de editar o texto do arquivo.' Creation mode re-derives the group's full SyMoleculeEntry[] the SAME way s1 does (syScanGroupMoleculeShortNames + syExtractTag + syExtractMoleculeDefs + syVaryingAxes/syPublishedLayout — all already pure, already exported, reused as-is) and calls syRenderIndexDefs again with identical project/purpose/usageContract/molecules and only `scenarios` replaced, then writes+compiles+re-caches the WHOLE index.defs.ts. This duplicates ~15 lines of s1's own extraction loop inside s3 rather than touching s1's file or its SyGroupArtifact contract (todo §0.4: don't reopen s1 without saying why) — the alternative (extending SyGroupArtifact to carry the full molecule list so s3 could read it back instead of re-deriving) would have required exactly that. Root now passes each s3 step the SAME purpose/usageContract it already gives that group's s1 step, so s3 does not need to re-read skills/index.ts either.
decisions.e8bCreation_tagAntiInvention: todo §4 item 3, and the family's honesty-over-invention rule applied for real this time (D-E3's version of it only ever DROPPED a foreign tag that already existed in another group's real catalog; here a hallucinated name would not exist ANYWHERE): every short name in a returned scenario's `recommended` is resolved against the group's own just-derived molecule list (helpers/syCreateIndexTs.syResolveCreationScenarios). A name that matches nothing is DROPPED, never guessed nor written, and recorded as a warning in the s3 artifact/report — mirroring D-E3's 'unmatched, left out, not invented' precedent rather than failing the whole attempt over one bad name.
decisions.e8bCreation_retryReusesN7Pattern: Gate failure or compile failure retries exactly like agentNewMolecule2/steps/n7-index: nmAgentStepIntent re-adds the step under planId `s3-<group>-retry<N>` (dependsOn nothing, runs immediately), capped at NM_MAX_ATTEMPTS (agentNewMolecule2/helpers/nmTypes.js, =3 — reused, not redefined). Every attempt's result step still emits the FIXED anchor syIndexTsDoneAnchor(canonical) on success, so s4's dependsOn (set once, at planting time) resolves regardless of which attempt succeeded. A retry hands the model back its own previous indexTs (readPreviousAttemptSource, same helper n7-index uses) plus the gate's rejection reasons, never a blind re-ask.
decisions.e8bCreation_indexTsNeverCached: index.ts (either mode) is never passed through syPublishToCache, matching E8a's existing behavior: nothing IMPORTS index.ts by name (it is the page a human opens directly, not a module another file resolves), so write+compile is the complete publish sequence for it — the same reasoning already recorded for s3's migration mode, just confirmed to also hold for creation. index.defs.ts (rewritten with the model's scenarios) DOES need syPublishToCache again, because index.ts imports IT by name and s1 already cached the pre-scenario version earlier in the same run.
decisions.e8bCreation_statusNaming: SyIndexTsArtifact.status gains 'created' alongside 'migrated'/'failed' (helpers/syTypes.ts) so a G1 group's outcome is distinguishable from a G3 group's in the same artifact shape, rather than overloading 'migrated' for two different operations. steps/s4-report/report.ts's SyIndexTsStatus drops the placeholder 'creation-needed' (it meant 'E8b not built' — no longer true) and gains 'created' / 'creation-failed'; the report's per-group branch for a G1 (creationSet) group now reads the s3 artifact the same way the G3/migration branch already does, instead of unconditionally returning a placeholder. SY_CREATION_NOT_BUILT and its summary line are removed for the same reason.

conventions.input: '@@agentSyncMoleculeCatalog [atualizar [grupo|grupos] <lista separada por vírgula/e ou all>] [incluindo o arquivo index.ts | com todos os arquivos]'. Parsed by helpers/syEntry (pure, no I/O). A mention that names the index page in an unrecognized way ('e a página do grupo', 'com o showcase') is REFUSED, naming the two recognized phrases — never silently interpreted either way. Since E8, the opt-in phrase no longer gates migration (decisions.migrationIsAutomatic) — it is parsed only because it still matters for a G1 group (creation, not built).
conventions.discovery: Group folders come from the project's OWN directories (helpers/syFs.syScanProjectGroupFolders — a stor scan), matched case-insensitively against skills/index.ts (the manual, editorial purpose-phrase registry). A folder with no skills/index.ts entry is IGNORED WITH A REASON, not skipped silently (D4) — today that is 'groupNavigateMain'.
conventions.artifactsAreTheContract: s2 and s4 read what s1/s3 already wrote to l4 (SyGroupArtifact / SyIndexTsArtifact), never a group's own index.defs.ts or index.ts source text — one source of truth per value.
conventions.writesNothingUnexpected: skill.ts, index.defs.ts, index.html — and now index.ts, but ONLY the renderReferenceTable() method plus two import lines (helpers/syMigrateIndexTs.syMigrateIndexTs) — never index.less, index.test.ts, or any usage.ts/creation.ts (manual, decision of 2026-08-17).

treeOverview: root (beforePromptImplicit, no LLM): parse the mention, scan the project, compute G1/G3 triggers, plant everything in one batch
s1-<group> x N   (code)  one index.defs.ts + index.html per matched group
s3-<group> x M   (code for G3 / one LLM call for G1)  migrates (G3) or creates (G1) index.ts for each triggered group, dependsOn its own s1 anchor
s2-project       (code)  skill.ts, dependsOn every s1 anchor
s4-report        (code)  report.json + readable summary, dependsOn s2 and every s3 anchor

steps.goal: For ONE group: read every molecule's .ts (tag) and .defs.ts (Objective, layoutConfig) if present; compute which layoutConfig axes vary across the siblings; resolve scenarios (preserve existing, else harvest from index.ts, else empty); render and write index.defs.ts + index.html.

steps.model: none for G3 (deterministic) — one tool-call turn for G1 (E8b)
steps.goal: Planted for a group with the G3 trigger (index.ts exists, not yet migrated) OR the G1 trigger (no index.ts at all). G3: replaces the whole renderReferenceTable() method body with a 3-line call into shared/indexReferenceTable.ts and adds the two imports it needs (helpers/syMigrateIndexTs) — no LLM. G1: one LLM tool-call turn writes the whole page ALREADY in that migrated shape (never hand-written markup — flow.json decisions.e8bCreation_pageIsBornMigrated) plus the scenarios as data, which this step then writes into the group's index.defs.ts (helpers/syCreateIndexTs, decisions.e8bCreation_rewriteViaRendererNotTextEdit). Never planted for a group with no trigger at all.
Read every s1 group artifact of this run's input.json list and render l2/molecules/skill.ts from them, alphabetical by folder.

Aggregate input.json + every s1/s2/s3 artifact into report.json and a readable summary: what was written, ignored groups with reasons, index.ts status PER GROUP (migrated / creation-needed / migration-failed / already-migrated), and that the catalog is written but not published.

output.result: the summary, in the step trace

artifacts.l4/agentSyncMoleculeCatalog/<runKey>/inp: the resolved run scope: matched/ignored/requested-but-ignored/unknown groups, indexTsMigrationGroups, indexTsCreationGroups

acceptance.e5RegenerationCheck: (E1-E7) Regenerating the 6 pilot groups from their real source files and diffing against the seeded v2 index.defs.ts: STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL for all 6. skill.ts: same `groups[]` entries and `Moléculas:` lines as SETS (order aside — decisions.groupOrder).
acceptance.e8aStrongAcceptance: (E8a, todo §3) Migrated groupEnterDate (4 molecules) and groupViewTable (12, the largest/most complex real index.ts at 796 lines) from their REAL current index.ts. Both: braces balanced after the surgery; hero/showcase cards/class declaration/render() left byte-identical; renderReferenceTable() collapsed to the 3-line delegate; the two new imports landed right after the last existing import. A scoped tsc compile of BOTH migrated files against real index.defs.ts content (regenerated for the check) and the real shared module: CLEAN, zero errors — including the cross-project mls-102040 -> mls-102020 import (s3Migration_D-E1_sharedModuleLocation). Reverted after the check; nothing in mls-102040 is committed by this agent's own work.
acceptance.tagResolution: Every tag in every artifact is read from a real @customElement decorator (helpers/syExtract.syExtractTag) — by construction, not by a post-hoc gate.
acceptance.noMoleculeDisappears: Every molecule file found under a group's folder appears in molecules[] — with defs:null and the out-of-contract markdown line when it has no .defs.ts.
acceptance.e8bStrongAcceptance: (E8b, todo §7 step 4) ⚠️ PENDING — needs a real Studio run, same as E8a's own T1 gate (testes-gerais.md): this is the first time this agent's own s3 step calls an LLM, and prompt/schema/gate correctness under a REAL model response has not been exercised. What IS verified without the LLM: the code compiles (scoped tsc, zero new errors), the pure helpers (syCreateIndexTs.syResolveCreationScenarios) and the structural gate (createGate.ts) pass their own unit tests against hand-written fixtures shaped like a real page, and a retry-routing bug (a failed attempt's speculatively-written index.ts made the NEXT attempt misroute into migration mode via nmFileExists) was found by code review and fixed before this line was written. Plan for the real run: create groupEnterDateTime's index.ts in mls-102040 (2 molecules, the smallest real G1 case) — see todo-implementar-E8b-criar-index-ts.md's own aceite forte.

outOfScope: n7-index / i6-index / v4-index and the two legacy agents (agentIndexGroupPage, agentUpdateIndexGroupPage) — excluding them is a decision for later, after this agent is proven
publishing the written catalog — no publish API exists on this platform (D5); the report says so every run
an agent-to-agent trigger from agentNewMolecule2/agentImproveMolecule2 into this one — depends on an unverified platform capability
recoloring the showcase CARDS (only the reference table is in play — todo §8) and normalizing intro prose beyond the title (D-E4)
planting: Single phase (see decisions.rootPlanting). The root's beforePromptImplicit does discovery + entry parsing + G1/G3 trigger detection itself and returns, in ONE batch: an add-message-ai intent with skipRootLLM:true (creates the step tree), one add-step per matched group (s1, status waiting_human_input), one add-step per G3-OR-G1-triggered group (s3, waiting_dependency on that group's own s1 anchor — same planting for both triggers since E8b, decisions.e8bCreation_targetChanged), s2 (waiting_dependency on every s1 anchor), s4 (waiting_dependency on s2's anchor plus every planted s3's anchor, G3 and G1 alike).
